libraries.name: GSAP core 3.13.0 (gsap, includes ScrollTrigger, Flip, SplitText)
libraries.neededFor: Every tween and timeline of the prototype: hero, memo, count, story, scrubbed rules timeline
libraries.license: npm: "Standard 'no charge' license: https://gsap.com/standard-license." (same on 3.15.1). The 3.13.0 tarball has no LICENSE file; text is on gsap.com (effective 30 Apr 2025, Webflow). Permitted on any website/web app; prohibited in no-code visual animation builders competing with Webflow; Webflow may terminate and amend. FAQ: commercial use free, plugins included. The old 'end users not charged' summary is commented out in the page source. Allows Leon (not an animation builder). Not open source; not legal advice.
libraries.canDrop: Mostly. Hero demo, entrances, memo, ticks, marks, terminal: CSS keyframes with animation-delay. Count-up, story, leave phase: Motion animate() (already installed, MIT). Keep GSAP only if the pinned scrub proves too fiddly with Motion scroll().

libraries.license: Same Standard 'no charge' license as gsap (same package).
libraries.canDrop: Yes, with work: position: sticky for the pin (main has overflow-x: clip, which keeps sticky working), Motion scroll() for the scrub, IntersectionObserver/Motion inView for once-on-enter. The frozen/slide/travel code disappears (no in-page anchors on the real home).

libraries.name: Motion 14.5.0 (already in package.json; framer-motion and motion-dom 14.5.0)
libraries.neededFor: The replacement for GSAP: animate(), scroll(), inView(), stagger, spring, hover, press (vanilla exports verified in node_modules); the app already uses motion/react
libraries.license: MIT (LICENSE.md: Copyright (c) 2024 Motion B.V.). Allows a commercial product.
libraries.canDrop: Not a drop: it is the no-new-dependency route. Its handling of CSS individual translate/rotate/scale properties (used across the kit) was not verified.

risks: Content, not only motion: the developers story (Evening/Night/Morning, sheets, thread, codex terminal), the rules' list of names, the mini documents, the 'dreaming' mark, a mark on the security heading and the close sign-up sheet do not exist in the real page or in messages/en.json and fr.json. Each needs a founder decision and new copy; do not port them silently.

Hydration flash and LCP: the SSR hero is painted before hydration (in next dev the CSS entrance has already finished at the load event). A JS sequence started at hydration would show a finished hero, hide it, replay it. Keep the headline and hero visible, stage the demo in CSS (starts at first paint), pre-hide with html.js-motion only what JS owns, keep the 3 s failsafe.

Double play: real CSS (s-arrive, s-rv view timelines on 14 nodes, s-land re-fired on every slot change, transitions) plus a JS port plays twice, and a running CSS animation overrides inline transform/opacity. Remove .s-rv/.s-arrive/.s-land from nodes that JS owns.
JS ignores data-motion=off: the global rule stops CSS only. Effects must read useInstant(), revert live (pin teardown shortens the page by about 1,700 px, re-measure) and re-run when switched back.

React owns the DOM: key remounts (question, view), a controlled switch, Strict Mode double effects, useLayoutEffect before paint, inline styles on React-managed nodes. Every setup must be revertable; kill tweens before a key remount; never write innerHTML.
Rule 3 privacy: Sophie's DOM must never contain Julie's email; keep one view rendered at a time and switch by state, not by cross-fading two views.

Pin geometry: fixed 72 px bar, main overflow-x: clip (must stay clip, hidden breaks sticky), rule heights 337 to 633 px by width, fragments of different heights stretched into one panel, pin only when a rule fits (h + 32 <= window height - bar); header/footer links go to other pages and the skip link to #contenu must keep working.

GSAP licence is permissive for Leon but not open source (terms editable and terminable by Webflow, no LICENSE file in the 3.13.0 tarball); adopting it also breaks the port brief (no new dependency) and brings the translate/rotate folding trap against a kit built on individual translate/rotate/scale. Motion's behaviour with those properties is not verified.

Prototype defects not to copy: 160 ms .hl colour fade blinking after a sweep (real .hl has the same transition), 3-line heading at 1024-1099 px when pinned, hero strokes at 0.2 s, GSAP transform folding, story terminal taller than a 900 px window.

Browser support: view()/scroll() timelines are @supports-guarded (Firefox without them shows the final state, same as today); @property --sweep is registered in kit.css. Nothing tested in Safari, Firefox, on a real touch device, with a trackpad or a screen reader; both films are Chrome headless at 1512x771.

DemoScene is mounted twice (hero and rule 1) with independent state: hero-only logic must be scoped to the hero instance; the pile is hidden under 1100 px so selection motion must check it is displayed.

Recommended order: (1) scaffolding; (2) hero demo + question switch + tab indicator + selection, mostly CSS; (3) ambient small wins (marks drawn on 7 headings, count 42, memo lines, ticks, footer, marquee tweaks); (4) rules pinned, after the founder rules on mini documents; (5) developers: terminal printing now, the 3-step story only once its copy is decided. Recommendation: no new dependency (CSS + motion already installed); if one library is wanted back, Rough Notation (MIT, 4 kB gzip) is the smallest.
